questions.question: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.explanation: Force is measured in newtons.

questions.question: Which quantity is the rate of change of velocity?
questions.explanation: Acceleration measures how quickly velocity changes.

questions.question: Which equation expresses Newton’s second law for constant mass?
questions.explanation: The resultant force equals mass multiplied by acceleration.

questions.question: Which force opposes sliding between two dry surfaces?
questions.explanation: Friction opposes relative sliding motion.

questions.question: What is inertia?
options: resistance to a change in motion
questions.explanation: Inertia is a body’s resistance to changes in its motion.

questions.question: A 2 kg trolley accelerates at 3 m/s². What is the resultant force?
questions.explanation: Using F = ma gives 2 × 3 = 6 N.

questions.question: A 12 N resultant force acts on a 4 kg object. What is its acceleration?
questions.explanation: Acceleration is F/m = 12/4 = 3 m/s².

questions.question: A body moves with constant velocity in a straight line. What is its resultant force?
questions.explanation: Constant velocity means zero acceleration and hence zero resultant force.

questions.question: Using g = 10 m/s², what is the weight of a 5 kg bag?
questions.explanation: Weight is mg = 5 × 10 = 50 N.

questions.question: A swimmer pushes water backwards. Why does the swimmer move forwards?
options: water exerts a forward reaction force
questions.explanation: Newton’s third law gives a forward force of water on the swimmer.

questions.question: Two horizontal forces of 9 N and 4 N act in opposite directions. What is their resultant?
questions.explanation: Opposing collinear forces subtract, giving 9 − 4 = 5 N.

questions.question: A 3 kg object has a 15 N forward pull and 6 N backward friction. What is its acceleration?
questions.explanation: The resultant is 9 N forwards, so a = 9/3 = 3 m/s² forwards.

questions.question: A vehicle speeds up uniformly from 4 m/s to 16 m/s in 6 s. What is its acceleration?
questions.explanation: Acceleration is (16 − 4)/6 = 2 m/s².

questions.question: A 2 kg object accelerates at 4 m/s² when pulled by 11 N. What frictional force opposes it?
questions.explanation: The resultant is 8 N, so opposing friction is 11 − 8 = 3 N.

questions.question: A 1,000 kg car accelerates at 1.5 m/s² against 500 N resistance. What is the driving force?
questions.explanation: Driving force minus 500 N equals ma = 1,500 N, so driving force is 2,000 N.

questions.question: Which structure controls most activities of a typical animal cell?
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains genetic material that controls cell activities.

questions.question: Which structure controls movement of substances into and out of a cell?
questions.explanation: The selectively permeable cell membrane regulates entry and exit.

questions.question: Which organelle carries out photosynthesis in green plant cells?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis.

questions.question: Which structure gives a plant cell support and a regular shape?
questions.explanation: The cellulose cell wall provides structural support.

questions.question: Where does most aerobic respiration occur in a typical eukaryotic cell?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria are the main site of aerobic respiration.

questions.question: Why do root hair cells have long projections?
options: to increase surface area for absorption
to store chromosomes outside the nucleus
questions.explanation: The projection increases the surface area for absorbing water and mineral ions.

questions.question: Which organelle joins amino acids to make proteins?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are the sites of protein synthesis.

questions.question: Which feature is typical of a bacterial cell?
options: DNA is not enclosed in a nucleus
a cellulose cell wall in every species
questions.explanation: Bacteria are prokaryotes and lack a membrane-bound nucleus.

questions.question: What happens when a healthy plant cell takes in water by osmosis?
options: the vacuole expands and the cell becomes turgid
questions.explanation: Water entering the vacuole creates turgor pressure against the cell wall.

questions.question: What is the function of a large central vacuole in a plant cell?
options: storing cell sap and helping maintain turgor
forming the cell membrane from cellulose
questions.explanation: The vacuole stores cell sap and helps keep the cell turgid.

questions.question: Why do muscle cells usually contain many mitochondria?
options: they need much energy for contraction
questions.explanation: Muscle contraction needs energy supplied by respiration in mitochondria.

questions.question: A cube-shaped cell has side length 2 units. What is its surface-area-to-volume ratio?
questions.explanation: Its surface area is 24 and volume is 8, giving a ratio of 3:1.

questions.question: Why does a smaller cell usually exchange materials more efficiently than a similar larger cell?
options: it has a larger surface-area-to-volume ratio
it has no need for nutrients
its volume always exceeds its surface area
its membrane is made of cellulose
questions.explanation: A larger surface-area-to-volume ratio supports exchange relative to the cell’s needs.

questions.question: A red blood cell placed in concentrated salt solution shrinks. What explains this?
options: the cell grows a cellulose wall
questions.explanation: Water moves out through the cell membrane into the more concentrated solution.

questions.question: A leaf cell cannot make enough proteins after damage to many ribosomes. Which process is directly affected?
questions.explanation: Damaged ribosomes directly reduce protein synthesis from amino acids.

questions.question: In economics, demand requires a desire for a good and what else?
questions.explanation: Effective demand combines desire with ability and willingness to pay.

questions.question: What does the law of demand normally predict when a good’s own price rises, other things equal?
questions.explanation: Other things equal, price and quantity demanded are inversely related.

questions.question: Which axis normally shows price on a demand graph?
questions.explanation: Price is normally plotted on the vertical axis.

questions.question: Which pair is an example of substitute goods?
questions.explanation: Tea and coffee can replace one another in consumption.

questions.question: Which pair is an example of complementary goods?
questions.explanation: Cars and petrol are commonly used together.

questions.question: What causes a movement along an unchanged demand curve?
options: a change in the good’s own price
questions.explanation: A change in own price changes quantity demanded along the same curve.

questions.question: Income rises and demand for a normal good increases. How does its demand curve move?
options: only down along the same curve
only up along the same curve
questions.explanation: Higher income shifts demand for a normal good to the right.

questions.question: Income rises and demand for an inferior good falls. What type of good is it?
questions.explanation: Demand for an inferior good decreases as income rises, other things equal.

questions.question: Coffee becomes more expensive. What may happen to demand for tea, a substitute?
questions.explanation: Some buyers switch from coffee to tea, increasing demand for tea.

questions.question: Petrol becomes more expensive. What may happen to demand for large petrol cars?
options: it equals the price of petrol
questions.explanation: Higher running costs can reduce demand for a complementary good such as a petrol car.

questions.question: Which change is most likely to increase market demand for notebooks?
options: notebooks become less useful to pupils
questions.explanation: More potential buyers can shift market demand for notebooks to the right.

questions.question: Price rises by 10% and quantity demanded falls by 20%. What is the magnitude of price elasticity of demand?
questions.explanation: The elasticity magnitude is 20%/10% = 2.

questions.question: Price falls by 5% and quantity demanded rises by 5%. What is the elasticity magnitude?
questions.explanation: Equal percentage changes give unit elasticity, with magnitude 1.

questions.question: A firm raises price and total revenue falls. What does this suggest about demand over that range?
questions.explanation: With elastic demand, the percentage fall in quantity outweighs the percentage price rise.

questions.question: At ₦100, 30 units are demanded; at ₦80, 40 units are demanded. What describes the change caused by this price fall alone?
options: an extension of demand along the curve
a decrease in demand to the left
a rise in the price of a substitute
questions.explanation: A fall in own price causes an extension in quantity demanded along the same curve.

questions.question: Which word is a noun in “The teacher smiled”?
questions.explanation: Teacher names a person and is a noun.

questions.question: Which word is the verb in “Ada studies every evening”?
questions.explanation: Studies expresses the action in the sentence.

questions.question: Which word is an adjective in “She carried a heavy bag”?
questions.explanation: Heavy describes the noun bag.

questions.question: Which word is an adverb in “Tunde answered politely”?
questions.explanation: Politely describes how Tunde answered.

questions.question: Which word is a pronoun in “They arrived early”?
questions.explanation: They stands in place of a noun or noun phrase.

questions.question: What part of speech is “under” in “The book is under the table”?
questions.explanation: Under shows the relationship between the book and the table.

questions.question: What part of speech is “and” in “Zainab and Chidi studied”?
questions.explanation: And joins the two names and is a conjunction.

questions.question: What does “very” modify in “The test was very difficult”?
questions.explanation: Very is an adverb modifying the adjective difficult.

questions.question: What part of speech is “hers” in “That calculator is hers”?
questions.explanation: Hers replaces a possessive noun phrase such as her calculator.

questions.question: What part of speech is “a” in “Funmi bought a pen”?
questions.explanation: A introduces a singular non-specific countable noun.

questions.question: What part of speech is “because” in “We stayed because it rained”?
questions.explanation: Because introduces a subordinate clause giving a reason.

questions.question: In “We study hard”, what part of speech is “hard”?
questions.explanation: Hard modifies the verb study and functions as an adverb here.

questions.question: In which sentence is “light” used as a verb?
questions.explanation: Light expresses the action of making the candle burn.

questions.question: In “Swimming keeps me fit”, how does “Swimming” function?
options: as a noun naming an activity
questions.explanation: Swimming is a gerund functioning as the subject noun.

questions.question: In “The very small child laughed loudly”, which pair consists only of adverbs?
questions.explanation: Very modifies small, and loudly modifies laughed, so both function as adverbs.
